name: Regional District of Nanaimo Stewardship Seed Funding
summary: Seed grants for volunteer-based non-profit stewardship groups restoring and enhancing creeks, streams, rivers, estuaries and wetlands within the Regional District of Nanaimo, British Columbia.

geography.label: Regional District of Nanaimo, British Columbia

eligibility.rule: Locate the project within the Regional District of Nanaimo
Actively enhance stream health, hydrology, or function
Be a volunteer-based, not-for-profit group pursuing direct-benefit projects
Project was not funded in each of the three previous years

calls.label: 2026 intake
calls.note: Limited funds each year; the page says when they run out

status.quote: currently accepting applications for project proposals for 2026

applicant_types.quote: it must be a volunteer-based, not-for-profit group that actively pursues the completion of restoration, research, and/or enhancement projects

geography.quote: be located within the Regional District of Nanaimo

amount.quote: Funding issued can be up to $10,000.

access.quote: Email or mail the completed form, supporting documents, and 'before' photos to waterstewardship@rdn.bc.ca

co_finance_required.quote: be jointly funded by other partners, donors, and/or include in-kind contributions

eligibility.quote: be located within the Regional District of Nanaimo
actively enhance stream health, hydrology, or function

volunteer-based, not-for-profit group that actively pursues the completion of restoration, research, and/or enhancement projects that are of direct benefit to a creek, stream, river, estuary, or wetland within the Regional District of Nanaimo.

After the third year of funding, the project is ineligible for funding for that following year. After a one-year grace period to allow others to access funds, the project is eligible to apply for funding again for up to three consecutive years.

documents.quote: To meet application requirements, you must include in one format or another an itemized breakdown of project costs and the reasoning the site(s) was/were chosen.
The Site Overview not only includes the current conditions of the site; it is the rationalization of why the site was chosen and further demonstrates the relevance of the project.
Location map of site, such as a RDN Map (www.rdn.bc.ca/gis-mapping) or Google Earth image.
